issue_context.title: test_runner: add coverage support with watch mode.
issue_context.body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

Currently, we can't get coverage report along with watch flag.

code:

```js
import test from "node:test";

test("foo", () => {});
```

run cmd `./node/node --test --watch --experimental-test-coverage`

output:

```bash
pulkitgupta@Pulkits-MacBook-Air jest-2 % ../node/node --test --watch --experimental-test-coverage
✔ foo (0.867791ms)
^C%                                                                                                                                                       
pulkitgupta@Pulkits-MacBook-Air jest-2 % 
```

no coverage report.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

To show test coverage with watch mode, (something similar what jest does).

output:
```bash
pulkitgupta@Pulkits-MacBook-Air jest-2 % ../node/node --test --watch --experimental-test-coverage  
✔ foo (1.044042ms)
ℹ start of coverage report
ℹ ---------------------------------------------------------------
ℹ file           | line % | branch % | funcs % | uncovered lines
ℹ ---------------------------------------------------------------
ℹ index.test.mjs | 100.00 |   100.00 |  100.00 | 
ℹ ---------------------------------------------------------------
ℹ all files      | 100.00 |   100.00 |  100.00 |
ℹ ---------------------------------------------------------------
ℹ end of coverage report
^C%  
```

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_
comments: what would be the trigger/point in time for the coverage report te be calculated?

> what would be the trigger/point in time for the coverage report te be calculated?

once all tests have completed.

I expected a similar behavior when I ran `node --watch --experimental-test-coverage index.test.mjs`.

> once all tests have completed.

they never complete, thats the point

review_comments: Why do you remove this flag here?

This will help to re-run the watching file with code coverage enabled ([filterExecArgv()](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/51288/files#diff-840cee72cdda14be90e6c5607ffa844eaf73be966607ddc834cc667bd142fb21R110-R113)). without this the watched file re-runs without code coverage.

for the initial run of all test files, the coverage is accumelated and printed by the orcastator process.
after the initial run ends - for every watched file, we pass `--experimental-test-coverage` so that the file calculates its individual coverage internally
